ei.title: When Space Enters the Sound's Route

fullPassage: Rooms have their own "sound" because they impose their own characteristics on audio signals contained within them. It's actually kind of remarkable. Sound such as music coming from headphones will sound the same everywhere. No matter what acoustical environment we are in, the headphones sound the same. That's because the room is not part of that playback signal path. But sound such as music from a loudspeaker will sound different in every acoustical environment. Every room where you set up the loudspeaker will cause the sound you hear to be different—sometimes dramatically different; that is because the room is now part of the signal path. Also, in the same room, the loudspeaker will sound different when it is placed in different locations in the room and it will sound different as you move around the room. Similarly, when you are recording a musical instrument, the sound you receive at the microphone will be different in every room and the recorded sound will sound different as the instrument or the microphone is moved.

questions.passage: Rooms have their own "sound" because they (A)[impose / remove] their own characteristics on audio signals contained within them. Sound such as music coming from headphones will sound the same everywhere. That's because the room is not part of that (B)[playback / recording] signal path. But sound such as music from a loudspeaker will sound (C)[different / identical] in every acoustical environment. That's because the room is not part of that playback signal path. But sound such as music from a loudspeaker will sound different in every acoustical environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 방은 오디오 신호에 자신의 특성을 부과한다(impose). 헤드폰은 방이 재생(playback) 신호 경로의 일부가 아니기 때문에 같게 들린다. 하지만 스피커 소리는 모든 환경에서 다르게(different) 들린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① impose — playback — different: 원문과 일치
❌ ② remove(제거하다): impose의 반의어
❌ ③ recording(녹음): playback과 다른 의미
❌ ④ identical(동일한): different의 반의어
det.tip: impose = 부과하다, playback = 재생, different = 다른

questions.passage: That's because the room is not part of that playback signal path. But sound such as music from a loudspeaker will sound different in every acoustical environment. Every room where you set up the loudspeaker will cause the sound you hear to be different—sometimes (A)[dramatically / slightly] different; that is because the room is now part of the signal path. Also, in the same room, the loudspeaker will sound different when it is (B)[placed / removed] in different locations and it will sound different as you (C)[move / stay] around the room. Similarly, when you are recording a musical instrument, the sound you receive at the microphone will be different in every room and the recorded sound will sound different as the instrument or the microphone is moved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 때때로 극적으로(dramatically) 다르게 들린다. 같은 방에서도 스피커가 다른 위치에 놓이면(placed) 다르게 들리고, 방을 돌아다니면(move) 다르게 들린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② dramatically — placed — move: 원문과 일치
❌ ① slightly(약간): dramatically와 다른 의미
❌ ③ removed(제거된): placed의 반의어
❌ ④ stay(머무르다): move의 반의어
det.tip: dramatically = 극적으로, place = 놓다, move around = 돌아다니다

questions.passage: It's actually kind of remarkable. Sound such as music coming from headphones will sound the same everywhere. No matter what acoustical (A)[environment / equipment] we are in, the headphones sound the same. But sound from a loudspeaker will sound different in every acoustical environment. Similarly, when you are (B)[recording / playing] a musical instrument, the sound you (C)[receive / produce] at the microphone will be different in every room. Every room where you set up the loudspeaker will cause the sound you hear to be different—sometimes dramatically different; that is because the room is now part of the signal path.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 음향 환경(environment)에 있든 헤드폰 소리는 같다. 악기를 녹음할(recording) 때 마이크에서 받는(receive) 소리는 방마다 다르다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ environment — recording — receive: 원문과 일치
❌ ① equipment(장비): environment와 다른 의미
❌ ② playing(연주하는): recording과 다른 의미
❌ ④ produce(생산하다): receive와 다른 의미
det.tip: acoustical environment = 음향 환경, record = 녹음하다, receive = 받다

questions.passage: Rooms have their own "sound" because they impose their own ①<u>characteristics</u> on audio signals contained within them. Sound such as music coming from headphones will sound the same everywhere. That's because the room is not part of that playback signal path. But sound such as music from a loudspeaker will sound ②<u>identical</u> in every acoustical environment. Every room where you set up the loudspeaker will cause the sound you hear to be different—sometimes ③<u>dramatically</u> different; that is because the room is now part of the ④<u>signal</u> path.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② identical(동일한) → different(다른): 스피커 소리는 모든 음향 환경에서 '다르게' 들린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① characteristics(특성): 원문 일치
❌ ② identical(동일한): 원문은 different(다른) — 반의어로 교체됨
✅ ③ dramatically(극적으로): 원문 일치
✅ ④ signal(신호): 원문 일치
det.tip: different(다른) ↔ identical(동일한)

questions.passage: Also, in the same room, the loudspeaker will sound different when it is ①<u>placed</u> in different locations in the room and it will sound different as you ②<u>move</u> around the room. Similarly, when you are ③<u>recording</u> a musical instrument, the sound you receive at the microphone will be ④<u>uniform</u> in every room and the recorded sound will sound different as the instrument or the microphone is moved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ uniform(균일한) → different(다른): 마이크에서 받는 소리는 모든 방에서 '다르다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① placed(놓인): 원문 일치
✅ ② move(움직이다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ recording(녹음하는): 원문 일치
❌ ④ uniform(균일한): 원문은 different(다른) — 반의어로 교체됨
det.tip: different(다른) ↔ uniform(균일한)

❌ ④ look into(조사하다): 다른 의미

det.analysis:

❌ ① ordinary(평범한): 반의어
❌ ② boring(지루한): 반의어
❌ ④ trivial(사소한): 반의어

questions.passage: But sound such as music from a loudspeaker will sound different in every acoustical environment. det.analysis:
❌ ④ slightly(약간): dramatically의 반의어 → 가장 먼 의미
✅ ① significantly(상당히): 유사어
✅ ② considerably(상당히): 유사어
✅ ③ remarkably(현저히): 유사어

questions.passage: Sound such as music coming from headphones will sound the same everywhere. No matter what <u>acoustical</u> environment we are in, the headphones sound the same. That's because the room is not part of that playback signal path. But sound such as music from a loudspeaker will sound different in every acoustical environment.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 acoustical과 관련된 의미로 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: acoustical = 음향의 ↔ visual = 시각의
det.analysis:
❌ ③ visual(시각의): acoustical(청각/음향)과 가장 먼 의미
✅ ① auditory(청각의): 동의어
✅ ② sonic(음파의): 유사어
✅ ④ aural(귀의): 동의어
det.tip: acoustical = auditory = aural = 음향의 ↔ visual = 시각의

questions.passage: Rooms have their own "sound" because they impose their own characteristics on audio signals contained within them. It's actually kind of remarkable. Sound such as music coming from headphones will <u>sound</u> the same everywhere.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 sound가 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: sound는 다의어: ① 소리(명사) ② ~하게 들리다(동사) ③ 건전한(형용사) ④ 울리다. 이 문맥에서는 '~하게 들리다'를 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ② be heard in a particular way(특정한 방식으로 들리다): sound the same = 같게 들리다
❌ ① a noise or vibration(소음이나 진동): 명사 의미
❌ ③ healthy and in good condition(건전한): 형용사 의미
❌ ④ to measure the depth of water(수심을 재다): 다른 동사 의미
det.tip: sound(동사) = ~하게 들리다 | sound the same = 같게 들리다

questions.stem:

❌ ① musical(음악의): 음악에 한정
❌ ② electrical(전기의): 다른 분야

det.analysis:

❌ ④ compose(구성하다): 만들다
det.tip: impose = 부과하다 (im- = in/on + pose = put)
